subject: Request for temporary uptime-floor reduction and monthly credit carveout
messages:
From: Luis Moreno <luis.moreno@orbitsoft.com>
To: ava_chen@redwood.ai
Cc: Karen Park <karen.park@orbitsoft.com>
Date: Tue, 17 Jun 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: temporary uptime-floor reduction and monthly credit carveout

Hi Ava,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team is excited about the latency numbers you showed. We got internal sign-off to move forward pending one operational ask from our security/compliance team.

Because OrbitSoft is migrating an on-prem ETL cluster over the next 8 weeks, our traffic profile will be spiky and we'll be operating behind a maintenance window that the SRE team cannot compress. The procurement team asked whether Redwood can: 1) temporarily lower the standard monthly uptime floor from 99.95% to 99.5% for the first two billing months, and 2) cap monthly service credits to a fixed-dollar amount (rather than percent-of-monthly-invoice) during that window.

Attached is our formal request (OrbitSoft_SLA_Request_v1.pdf) with the rationale and timeline. We appreciate a quick run at whether this is something Redwood would consider and, if so, a proposed redline.

Best,
Luis
Luis Moreno
Head of Cloud Ops, OrbitSoft
luis.moreno@orbitsoft.com
+1 (415) 555-0123

From: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.ai>
To: Luis Moreno <luis.moreno@orbitsoft.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 17 Jun 2025 12:25:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: temporary uptime-floor reduction and monthly credit carveout

Hi Luis — thanks for the clear ask and the PDF. We're happy OrbitSoft had a good experience on the demo.

Short answer: we can consider a temporary adjustment, but we need to align on two things before I put a formal redline on paper:
- A clearly scoped timebox (you mentioned 8 weeks — can you confirm start/end dates).
- A fixed-dollar cap proposal from you so we can run the economics vs. the fairness guardrails we have for other customers.

Ben, looping you in on pricing guardrails; Laura, can you review for legal risk if we provide an exception and a fixed-dollar cap (will likely require a one-off amendment). Aditya — please flag any operational/ops reasons this would be hard to support (e.g., routing/fallback changes, burst capacity exposure).

Luis — if you can confirm the dates and propose a cap today, I can have a draft amendment back to you by EOD tomorrow.

Thanks,
Ava Chen
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
ava_chen@redwood.ai
Attachments: None

From: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.ai>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai, aditya_rao@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 17 Jun 2025 14:01:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Request: temporary uptime-floor reduction and monthly credit carveout

Team — forwarding OrbitSoft's ask. Key pieces: temporary uptime floor -> 99.5% for two billing cycles, and cap credits to a fixed-dollar amount (they suggested $12,500/month in the call).

My assessment: strategic mid-market ACV (~$210k ARR); high likelihood to convert quickly once this is in contract. Risk areas:
- Legal: one-off amendment and how this interacts with standard SLAs (need to ensure no precedence across our mid-market tier).
- Pricing: Ben, confirm whether $12.5k/month is acceptable given projected MRC.
- Engineering/OPS: Aditya — do we have any constraints implementing a timeboxed lower floor? Would this require a special routing policy or flag in the console?

Please reply inline with redlines or concerns. I'm planning to respond to Luis with a draft by tomorrow EOD.

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>

Cc: Luis Moreno <luis.moreno@orbitsoft.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Jun 2025 08:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: temporary uptime-floor reduction and monthly credit carveout

Thanks for looping me in. Quick operational read: the platform can support a temporary contract-level uptime adjustment without code changes — we track SLOs per-customer and can set the floor to 99.5% for the defined billing periods. A couple of notes:

1) Metric scope: we need to confirm whether OrbitSoft's ask is for the hosted API endpoints only (recommended) or for Dedicated/private routing variants as well. The latter increases risk and may require additional isolation.
2) Measurement window: if we apply a lower floor for "billing cycle X and Y" we need to specify the exact UTC boundaries (we should propose local UTC-aligned billing cutover times).
3) Credit calc: fixed-dollar caps are operationally easy to report, but legal needs to sign off — Ben/Laura, if we accept $12,500/month cap, my view is that we should reserve the right to exclude maintenance windows we schedule that are communicated 72 hours in advance.

I attached a quick proposed redline (RI-proposed-sla-redline.docx) that: a) reduces the uptime floor to 99.5% for 2025-07-01 through 2025-08-31, b) limits monthly credits to $12,500 during that window, and c) adds a maintenance carveout (72h notice) and an explicit one-off amendment clause so this doesn't become precedent.

If legal and pricing are OK, Ava — send this as a draft amendment; suggest we mark it as "Pilot Exception — OrbitSoft" so it stays discrete.

-Aditya
Aditya Rao
Sr. Site Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference
